def-emx-lorentz-star:
## Definition

Let $V=\mathbb R^4$ with ordered coframe $e^0=dx^0,e^1=dx^1,e^2=dx^2,e^3=dx^3$, bilinear form $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, inverse $\eta^{-1}=\eta$, and volume form $\mathrm{vol}_\eta=e^0\wedge e^1\wedge e^2\wedge e^3$. For $0\le k\le4$, give $\Lambda^kV^*$ the induced bilinear pairing $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_\eta:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{\mu_1\cdots\mu_k}\beta^{\mu_1\cdots\mu_k}$, with indices raised by $\eta^{-1}$. The Lorentzian Hodge star is the unique linear map $\star_\eta:\Lambda^kV^*\to\Lambda^{4-k}V^*$ satisfying $\alpha\wedge\star_\eta\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_\eta\,\mathrm{vol}_\eta$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Lambda^kV^*$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, write $e^I$ for the corresponding wedge, $I^c$ for its increasing complement, $s(I,I^c)$ for the sign of the concatenation $(I,I^c)$ relative to $(0,1,2,3)$, and $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$, where $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. The equivalent basis formula is $\star_\eta e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}$.

For a smooth manifold $N$, an integer $1\le k\le\dim N$, a smooth closed $k$-form $\omega\in\Omega^k(N)$, and a finite real smooth singular $k$-cycle $z=\sum_\sigma c_\sigma\sigma$ with $\partial z=0$, define its period by $\operatorname{Per}_z(\omega):=\int_z\omega:=\sum_\sigma c_\sigma\int_\sigma\omega$. The form $\omega$ is exact when $\omega=d\alpha$ for a globally defined smooth $(k-1)$-form $\alpha\in\Omega^{k-1}(N)$. These are mathematical definitions and use no physical constants.
lem-emx-unit-sphere-radial-flux:
## Statement

Let $S^2=\{p\in\mathbb R^3:\|p\|_2=1\}$ have its standard embedded smooth structure and outward orientation, let $X(p)=p$, and let $\omega$ be its outward area form, $\omega_p(v,w)=p\cdot(v\times w)$ for tangent vectors $v,w\in T_pS^2$. Put $D=[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ and
$$
\Phi(\theta,\phi)=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta).
$$
The map $\Phi$ presents $S^2$ as a regular parametrized surface patch, with boundary seam and poles allowed by the patch convention. The outward flux of $X$ is
$$
\int_D (X\circ\Phi)\cdot(\Phi_\theta\times\Phi_\phi)\,d\theta\,d\phi=4\pi.
$$
Equivalently, the oriented top-form integral is $\int_{S^2}\omega=4\pi$.
lem-emx-lorentz-star-square:
## Statement

For the orientation and signature $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ fixed in [[def-emx-lorentz-star]], the Hodge star satisfies $\star_\eta^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}$ on $k$-forms, $0\le k\le4$. In particular, on two-forms $\star_\eta^2=-\operatorname{id}$, $\star_\eta(dx^0\wedge dx^1)=-dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and $\star_\eta(dx^2\wedge dx^3)=dx^0\wedge dx^1$.
thm-emx-local-potential-homotopy:
## Statement

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open and star-shaped about $a\in U$, meaning $a+t(x-a)\in U$ for every $x\in U$ and $t\in[0,1]$. For a smooth closed two-form $F=\frac12F_{\mu\nu}\,dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu$ on $U$, define the smooth one-form $A=A_\mu dx^\mu$ by

$$A_\mu(x)=\int_0^1 t(x-a)^\nu F_{\nu\mu}(a+t(x-a))\,dt.$$

Then $dA=F$. On any smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, a smooth closed two-form $F$ has a globally defined smooth one-form potential $A$ with $dA=F$ if and only if its de Rham class $[F]\in H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$ is zero. If a finite smooth singular two-cycle $z$ has nonzero period $\int_zF$, then $F$ is not globally exact.
